main_text.p: aurium dolore, ὠπαλγία[?] dicto, patet, quem sanguis tenuis biliosus plerunque concitat. Eadem dentium ratio, nam quanquam dentibus nullus insit sensus; (quicquid reclamet Trallianus) eorum tamen radicibus inserti sunt nervuli, quos calidus humor, aut alioqui aër, irritare solet. Non nego, quin frigida intemperies sola, eundem dolorem paritura sit; verum sepissimè adjunctum habet similem humorem.

Huc pertinet Arthritis, articulorum dolor, per intervalla affligens ex humoris defluxu. Articuli secundum omnes partes non dolent, sed partes sensiles nervosas; tendines nimirum musculorum, membranas, cutem: ligamenta enim, cartilagines, & ossa sensu destituuntur. Humor itaque descendens, prædictas partes divellit & distendit. Jam vero antea monui, in omni fluxione humorum quatuor esse consideranda, terminus quo, & ad quem, viam & materiam. Terminus ad quem est articulus af

page.notes: The right-hand strip (faint, cropped, partly mirrored) belongs to the facing page and is show-through or the neighbouring page's margin; no marginal notes of this page are legible, so none are transcribed. The Greek word ὠπαλγία is uncertain in its accents and final letter. The final word "af" is continued by the catchword "fectus" at the right foot.
